comment: Hand-written cases outside the trace fixtures. Every trace in tests/fixtures/harness*/ is a case 'trace/<name>' added by the generator. Kinds: official_trace (recorded on the official server and replayed by Circuit), black_box (the same client script against the official server and Circuit, outputs compared), real_client (the unmodified client against Circuit only), round_trip (data through the official server and back), planned (an acceptance case with no expectation recorded yet).

cases.description: 48 steps: every click mode in a chest, the own window, a double chest and a hopper, throws and pickups
Wall correction, falls, regeneration, death, respawn, the void and the floating kick
19 moves against a chest, repeaters, a hopper and a full block
Seven chest placement and pairing cases
Player placement of dust, levers, a step, a wall lever and repeaters
Six pass/fail checks calibrated on the official server, then run against Circuit
66 steps of walking, jumping, sprinting, falling, death and respawning
Repeater lines, pistons and a second player
A world exported by Circuit, opened and saved by the official server, imported again
TNT placement, breaking and every ignition path
Primed TNT creation order, fuse, motion, collision and removal
Primed TNT on the ground, in the air, in water and at chunk edges
Explosion blocks, drops, chain reactions, damage and knockback, also submerged
Live fuses across save, reload and unload
The tntExplodes game rule on and off (1.21.8 only)
A named TNT duplication design over repeated cycles
The duplication machine at chunk edges and corners, across region changes and restarts

Item stacks with components that the official servers sent after /give: 36 stacks with 93 of 96 component types (1.21.8) and 31 with 65 of 67 (1.21.4) are read, checked, written back in canonical form and read again (protocol_tests)
Creative slots with a custom name and a potion are kept and sent back with their components; an enchanted book is refused because the enchantment registry is not synchronized

A world saved by the official server with a named chest, items with a custom name, lore, damage, rarity and glint, and a sign with text: imported by Circuit, shown to a client with the chest title and the components, exported and read back by the official server unchanged; a second world with a trimmed chestplate and a banner with patterns and a base color likewise

Every registry Circuit synchronizes has the same entries as the official server's configuration, and the bundles' game rules are the official /gamerule lists (server_tests); registries not sent are listed

cases.location: tests/data/data_tests.cpp with the operator's jars; external: client harness smoke with vanilla-server-jar
cases.description: The official jars' built-in packs load (SHA-1 and version.json checked); each registry Circuit numbers has as many tags as the official servers send; the unmodified clients of both versions join with the enchantment registry and every tag; enchanted items round-trip through Anvil and the official server

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/craft-loot.js (craft); tests/fixtures/crafting/own-window.tsv, replayed by tests/server/server_tests.cpp with the operator's 1.21.8 jar
cases.description: 48 steps in the own window: results following the grid, taking them by click, right click, shift-click (also with room for part of the result), number key and throwing, mirrored shapes, honey bottle remainders, transmuting a shulker box and refusing to transmute a box into itself; Circuit and both official servers give identical windows

cases.location: tests/fixtures/loot/block-drops.tsv, checked by tests/server/server_tests.cpp with the operator's jars; external: circuit-clienttest/craft-loot.js (place, dig)
cases.description: 23 blocks and tools per version broken on the official servers; Circuit drops the same items in the 19 cases whose tables are deterministic (on 1.21.8 also live, from the imported world), and nothing in the 4 that draw random numbers

cases.location: external: circuit-harness/experiments/c22 (forced rings, spawn radius, idle level) and circuit-clienttest/ticking.js
cases.description: What each chunk level runs, the start ticket's level for each spawnChunkRadius, the idle-level rule and where random ticks run, observed on both official servers. Circuit does not compare these recordings: they observe chunk-loading timing that varies between runs, random ticks and spawnChunkRadius changes; trace/ring_blocks and trace/unload_reload compare the repeatable part

cases.location: tests/fixtures/light/, checked by tests/evidence/evidence_tests.cpp; external: circuit-harness light report
cases.description: Emission, dampening and light occlusion shape of every block state, reported by both official servers (27,946 states of 1.21.8, 27,866 of 1.21.4, identical where both have them); Circuit's table matches every one

cases.location: tests/fixtures/collision/, checked by tests/evidence/evidence_tests.cpp; external: circuit-harness collision report
cases.description: The collision boxes of every block state without an entity context, reported by both official servers (27,946 states of 1.21.8, 27,866 of 1.21.4); Circuit's boxes, which items and players move against, match every one through its own state representation

cases.location: tests/fixtures/collision/replaceable-*.txt, checked by tests/evidence/evidence_tests.cpp; external: circuit-harness collision report
cases.description: Which block states can be replaced and which a falling block falls into, reported by both official servers for every state (the same states, a whole block at a time); Circuit's rule matches every one

cases.location: tests/fixtures/collision/resistance-*.txt, checked by tests/evidence/evidence_tests.cpp; external: circuit-harness collision report
cases.description: The blast resistance of every block, reported by both official servers (1,105 blocks of 1.21.8, 1,095 of 1.21.4); Circuit's registry matches every one

cases.location: tests/fixtures/heightmap/, checked by tests/evidence/evidence_tests.cpp; external: circuit-harness heightmap report
cases.description: Whether every block state counts for MOTION_BLOCKING, reported by both official servers (27,946 states of 1.21.8, 27,866 of 1.21.4, identical where both have them); Circuit's rules match every one, and MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES is the same without leaves on both

35 test columns built with /setblock on the official 1.21.8 server (torches, dust, signs, carpets, candles, lanterns, open fence gates, slabs, leaves over stone and others), the world imported into Circuit through Anvil: the WORLD_SURFACE, MOTION_BLOCKING and MOTION_BLOCKING_NO_LEAVES heightmaps both servers send for the chunk are identical

The unmodified client builds a lit lamp and a stone overhang with a glass pane, then joins again so that its light comes from the server's chunk data; the light it holds at 14 positions is identical with the official server and with Circuit, in both runs, on both versions

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/gamerule-compare.js; Circuit's side also in tests/server/server_tests.cpp
cases.description: 45 /gamerule commands (queries, sets, bounds, malformed integers and booleans, quoted values, unknown and experimental rules, extra arguments and spaces) sent by a protocol client; Circuit's replies, as text components, are identical with each official server's, error context lines included

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/packet-probe.js with time-probe.txt and time-compare.txt; Circuit's side also in tests/server/server_tests.cpp
cases.description: 59 /time commands (set, add and query; markers, units, rounding, saturation, malformed times and extra arguments) with the daylight cycle stopped, then resumed, sent by a protocol client; Circuit's 144 reply lines and its sequence of set_time values are identical with each official server's, periodic set_time packets come at the same ages, and time advances again after the cycle resumes

cases.location: external: circuit-clienttest/packet-probe.js with weather-compare.txt, weather-join2.txt and (official only) weather-probe.txt, weather-timers.txt and weather-clear1.txt; Circuit's side also in tests/server/server_tests.cpp
cases.description: 16 /weather commands and a doWeatherCycle change, each from settled levels (rain, clear spells ending in thunderstorms, the cycle stopped, malformed durations), and a player joining in the rain: Circuit's 1,348 replies and game events per segment, every rain and thunder level value included, are identical with each official server's. The official servers' saved level data showed what each command does to the timers
